candidates.name: Nitzana Gas Pipeline — Egyptian section (Nitzana border to national grid)
aka: Egyptian internal pipeline for additional Israeli gas
candidates.sponsor: GASCO (Egyptian government); East Mediterranean Gas (EMG) reported negotiating a ~$300M loan for a new Sinai line
candidates.from: Nitzana border crossing (Egypt-Israel border, eastern Sinai)
candidates.to: Egyptian national gas grid via northern Sinai (Arish area)

evidence.note: Egypt to build a ~$400M pipeline located entirely within Egyptian territory, managed by GASCO, construction planned from Q4 2025 and completion by 2028, to receive the additional 130 bcm NewMed/Leviathan volumes.

Chevron/INGL FID on the Israeli Nitzana line (Ramat Hovav to Nitzana, 65 km, ~600 MMcf/d, complete 2028); Egypt separately to invest $400M to build the pipeline on its side of the border, with GASCO overseeing.
Arabic (attaqa.net): the expanded Israel-Egypt gas deal supports building a new pipeline; a local bank and East Mediterranean Gas negotiating a ~$300M loan to finance a new pipeline inside Sinai.

candidates.why_maybe_new: The roster appears to carry the ISRAELI side of this corridor twice (P3620 Israel-Egypt Onshore Gas Pipeline, Ramat Hovav->?, 65 km, construction; P7864 Nitzana Pipeline, 65 km, 36in, 600 MMcf/d, proposed) but no Egyptian-side segment from the Nitzana border into the Egyptian grid. The $400M GASCO-built line entirely within Egypt looks like a distinct, missing row - unless P3620's scope was intended to cover both sides of the border (consolidator to decide).

candidates.name: Ain Sokhna FSRU gas import pipeline (Sonker berth to national grid)
candidates.from: Sonker berth, Ain Sokhna port (FSRU regasification)
candidates.to: Egyptian national gas grid (Ain Sokhna / Suez Gulf area)

evidence.note: A 36-inch, 17-km gas import pipeline being installed at Sonker port as conduit for the third FSRU; Petrojet executing with GASCO engineering; two high-capacity marine and onshore pipelines built at SUMED and Sonker ports to connect FSRUs to the national grid.

Energos Eskimo FSRU nearing grid connection at SUMED berth, Ain Sokhna; new GASCO-built infrastructure injecting regasified LNG into the national grid (FSRUs operational mid-2025, so line may now be operating).

candidates.why_maybe_new: No Sokhna / Gulf of Suez FSRU-connector pipeline exists anywhere in the roster. At 17 km and 36-inch it is transmission-scale new-build (2024-2025), not in-plant piping; borderline terminal-connector classification - consolidator to decide whether GEM tracks it as a pipeline row or as part of the Ain Sokhna FSRU terminal entry.
